title: Fortifying the cities
summary: Moroni directs his armies to build earthworks, timber walls, pickets, towers, and protected positions around the cities.

explicit_facts.text: Moroni caused his armies to dig earthworks around the cities throughout the Nephite lands.
Timbers, strong high pickets, towers, and protected places were built around the cities.
The defenders could cast stones from the towers at those approaching the city walls.
Moroni prepared strongholds against enemies around every city in the land.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Construction crews work on defensive earthworks and wooden fortifications; no particular tools or uniforms are specified.
unspecified_visual_details: The cities' architecture, landscape, construction tools, and the defenders' clothing.

narration.text: Moroni did prepare strongholds against the coming of their enemies

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict an enemy attack; the verses describe preparations, not a battle here.

title: Driving the Lamanites south
summary: Moroni's armies enter the east wilderness and drive the Lamanites there into their own lands south of Zarahemla; the narration describes the course of the land of Nephi.

explicit_facts.text: Moroni sent his armies into the east wilderness, where they drove the Lamanites into their own lands south of Zarahemla.
The land of Nephi ran in a straight course from the east sea to the west.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The armies advance through a wilderness as the Lamanites retreat; the text does not specify combat.
unspecified_visual_details: The terrain, army formations, and how the expulsion occurred.

narration.text: they went forth and drove all the Lamanites who were in the east wilderness

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Verse 8 is geographic narration, not a separate visible event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a battle or specific route beyond what the verses state.

title: Settling the east wilderness
summary: After the Lamanites are driven out, inhabitants of Zarahemla and nearby lands go to possess the east wilderness by the seashore; armies fortify the southern borders.

explicit_facts.text: Moroni sent inhabitants of Zarahemla and nearby lands into the east wilderness to possess it as far as the seashore.
Armies were placed on the south borders and built fortifications for their protection.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Settlers move into the eastern territory; soldiers construct defensive works on the southern border.
unspecified_visual_details: The settlers' activities, fortification design, and the appearance of the seashore.

narration.text: go forth into the east wilderness, even to the borders by the seashore

prohibited_inventions: Do not show Lamanites present in the east wilderness after they were driven out.

title: A fortified boundary
summary: Moroni's forces fortify the boundary between Nephite and Lamanite lands; their numbers increase as the defenses reassure them.

explicit_facts.text: Moroni's forces cut off Lamanite strongholds in the east and west and fortified the boundary from the west sea by the head of the river Sidon.
Moroni's armies increased daily because the people were assured of protection by the works.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Soldiers work along a fortified boundary; the expanding force is shown gathered nearby.
unspecified_visual_details: The form and precise course of the fortifications, and the river's appearance.

narration.text: the Nephites possessing all the land northward

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a battle or claim the boundary was an impenetrable wall.

title: New city foundations
summary: The Nephites begin foundations for Moroni, Nephihah, and Lehi, as well as many other northern cities.

explicit_facts.text: The Nephites began a city called Moroni by the east sea, south of the Lamanite possessions.
They began a city or land called Nephihah between Moroni and Aaron, joining their borders.
They began many northern cities, including Lehi near the northern seashore.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Settlers begin laying city foundations, with coastal terrain in view.
unspecified_visual_details: The appearance and layout of the foundations and cities.

narration.text: they called the name of the city Moroni

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verses describe beginnings of foundations, not completed cities.
prohibited_inventions: Do not portray any named city as already built or populated.

title: Prosperity and the promise
summary: As the twenty-first year begins, the Nephites prosper and grow strong. The narration recalls the Lord's promise to Lehi about obedience and prosperity in the land.

explicit_facts.text: The twentieth year ended, and the twenty-first year began in prosperous circumstances for the Nephites.
The people prospered, became rich, multiplied, and grew strong in the land.
The narrator says the Lord's words to Lehi were being fulfilled: obedience brings prosperity in the land; disobedience means being cut off from the Lord's presence.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A prosperous community may be shown in ordinary settled life; no particular activity is specified.
unspecified_visual_details: The people's clothing, possessions, buildings, and daily activities.

narration.text: they shall be blessed, inasmuch as they shall keep my commandments they shall prosper in the land.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The promise is quoted as narration; Lehi and the Lord are not shown as present in this time.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the ancient utterance as a present event or invent a vision or divine appearance.

title: Consequences of wickedness
summary: The narrator attributes the Nephites' wars and destructions to internal sins and contrasts the faithful who were delivered with thousands who suffered bondage, death by the sword, or unbelief.

explicit_facts.text: The narrator says quarrels, contentions, murders, plunderings, idolatry, whoredoms, and abominations among the Nephites brought wars and destructions.
The faithful were delivered, while thousands of wicked people were consigned to bondage, perished by the sword, or dwindled in unbelief and mingled with the Lamanites.

unspecified_visual_details: The described past events are summarized, with no particular moment or setting supplied.

narration.text: it has been their quarrelings and their contentions
those who were faithful in keeping the commandments of the Lord were delivered at all times

doctrinal_or_story_notes: These verses summarize outcomes and causes rather than narrating a specific present event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not create a specific battle, death, captivity episode, or visible scene from the summarized events.

title: A time of happiness
summary: The narrator says there had never been a happier time among the Nephites since Nephi's days. The twenty-second and twenty-third years also ended in peace.

explicit_facts.text: The narrator calls Moroni's twenty-first year the happiest time among the Nephites since Nephi's days.
The twenty-second and twenty-third years ended in peace.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The people may be shown in a peaceful communal setting, without implying a specific celebration.
unspecified_visual_details: What the people are doing and the appearance of their surroundings.

narration.text: there never was a happier time among the people of Nephi

prohibited_inventions: Do not show Nephi or invent a specific celebration.

title: Contention over Lehi and Morianton
summary: In the twenty-fourth year, a land dispute arises between the people of Lehi and Morianton. Morianton's people take up arms, intent on killing their brethren.

explicit_facts.text: The lands of Lehi and Morianton bordered one another by the seashore, and contention arose over them.
The people of Morianton claimed part of Lehi's land, took up arms, and were determined to kill the people of Lehi by the sword.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The armed people of Morianton face the direction of Lehi's land; no fighting is yet described.
unspecified_visual_details: The boundary, weapons, and appearance of the neighboring lands.

narration.text: the people of Morianton took up arms against their brethren

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict combat yet; the verse says they were determined to fight.

title: The people of Lehi seek help
summary: The people of Lehi flee to Moroni's camp and appeal for help. Morianton's people learn of their flight and fear Moroni's army will attack them.

explicit_facts.text: The people of Lehi fled to Moroni's camp and appealed for assistance.
Morianton's people found out that the people of Lehi had fled and feared Moroni's army would come and destroy them.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The people of Lehi arrive at the camp; Morianton's people's fear can be conveyed through their expressions.
unspecified_visual_details: The camp's layout, the appeal's manner, and the group's specific expressions.

narration.text: the people who possessed the land of Lehi fled to the camp of Moroni

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The fear is reported; no attack by Moroni's army occurs in these verses.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent spoken words for the appeal or show Moroni's army attacking Morianton's people.

title: Morianton plans to flee north
summary: Morianton puts it into his people's hearts to flee north and take possession of the land there. In a separate incident, he becomes angry with a maidservant and beats her.

explicit_facts.text: Morianton urged his people to flee to and take possession of the land northward, which was covered with large bodies of water.
Morianton, described as a man of much passion, became angry with one of his maidservants and beat her much.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The first verse supports Morianton among his people; the second supports the assault as it happens, without showing injury.
unspecified_visual_details: The maidservant's identity and appearance, and the precise setting of either event.

narration.text: Morianton put it into their hearts that they should flee

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The planned flight and the assault are separate moments; do not combine them in one image.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show wounds, blood, or additional violence beyond the described beating.

title: The maidservant warns Moroni
summary: The maidservant flees to Moroni's camp and tells him about the beating and the plan to flee north. Moroni fears the consequences if Morianton's people gain the territory.

explicit_facts.text: The maidservant fled to Moroni's camp and told him about the matter and Morianton's people's intention to flee north.
Moroni feared that Morianton's people might join his people and gain territory, threatening Nephite liberty.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The maidservant can be shown reporting to Moroni; his concern may be shown through his expression.
unspecified_visual_details: The precise words spoken, their gestures, and Moroni's camp arrangements.

narration.text: she fled, and came over to the camp of Moroni

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The maidservant's report is summarized; the source supplies no direct dialogue.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent dialogue or depict Moroni's fear as a supernatural vision.

title: An army sent to block the flight
summary: Moroni sends an army with its camp to intercept Morianton's people. The army heads them off at the borders of Desolation by the narrow pass beside the sea.
locations: narrow pass by the sea at the borders of Desolation

explicit_facts.text: Moroni sent an army with its camp to head off Morianton's people and stop their flight north.
The army intercepted them at the borders of Desolation by the narrow pass leading beside the sea into the land northward.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The army blocks the narrow passage as Morianton's people arrive; the passage lies beside the sea.
unspecified_visual_details: The pass's shape, the sea's appearance, and the army's formation.

narration.text: there they did head them, by the narrow pass

prohibited_inventions: Do not show battle yet; the encounter and battle are described in the next verse.

title: Teancum defeats Morianton
summary: Teancum leads Moroni's army against Morianton's people. A battle begins; Teancum kills Morianton, defeats his army, takes the people prisoner, and returns to Moroni's camp.

explicit_facts.text: Moroni's army, led by Teancum, met Morianton's people and a battle began.
Teancum killed Morianton, defeated his army, took them prisoners, and returned to Moroni's camp.
The twenty-fourth year ended.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Show the battle in progress, with Teancum's action against Morianton; keep the depiction non-graphic.
unspecified_visual_details: Weapons, formations, terrain details, and how prisoners are guarded.
doctrinal_or_story_notes: The battle's outcome and the return are part of this narrated episode; avoid gore.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show blood, wounds, severed body parts, or unsourced dialogue.

title: The people are restored to their lands
summary: Morianton's people are brought back. After covenanting to keep the peace, they are restored to Morianton, and a union takes place with the people of Lehi, who are also restored to their lands.

explicit_facts.text: Morianton's people were brought back and restored to Morianton after covenanting to keep the peace.
A union took place between them and the people of Lehi, and both were restored to their lands.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Represent the restoration and union as the two groups together in a peaceful setting.
unspecified_visual_details: The covenant's form, the union's ceremony, and any individual participants.

narration.text: upon their covenanting to keep the peace they were restored

prohibited_inventions: Do not invent the terms of the covenant or a marriage or political ceremony.

title: Nephihah dies
summary: Nephihah dies after serving uprightly as chief judge. The narrator recounts that he had refused Alma the sacred records, which Alma had conferred upon his son Helaman.

explicit_facts.text: Nephihah died in the same year peace was restored, having filled the judgment-seat with perfect uprightness before God.
Nephihah had refused Alma possession of the sacred records; Alma had conferred them upon his son Helaman.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Nephihah may be shown as deceased, but no manner or setting of death is specified.
unspecified_visual_details: Nephihah's age, appearance, manner of death, and where it occurred.

narration.text: Nephihah, the second chief judge, died

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Verse 38 recounts an earlier transfer of records; it is not necessarily a present event alongside Nephihah's death.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show a deathbed, the record transfer as happening now, or any appearance not specified.

title: Pahoran appointed chief judge
summary: Nephihah's son is appointed chief judge and governor with an oath and sacred ordinance. He is named Pahoran and succeeds his father at the end of the twenty-fourth year.

explicit_facts.text: Nephihah's son was appointed chief judge and governor in his father's place, with an oath and sacred ordinance.
His name was Pahoran, and he began his reign at the end of the twenty-fourth year.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Pahoran is present at an appointment or oath-taking; the text supports the oath and ordinance but gives no staging details.
unspecified_visual_details: The appearance of the ordinance, witnesses, clothing, and location.
doctrinal_or_story_notes: The duties listed in verse 39 are summarized commitments, not supplied direct dialogue.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent oath wording, a crowd, or a specific ceremonial setting.
